A1.justification: Both PDFs describe EchoVLM and retain the same core research framework. All 20 pages of v1 and 23 pages of v2, including appendix tables, figures and image-only pages, support comparison through text extraction and visual inspection.

before.justification: V1 reports original report-generation, diagnosis and VQA experiments, ablations, routing analyses and clinical case comparisons.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds results for further baselines, a smaller model, medical entity evaluation and external ultrasound data.

M1.justification: The core Dual-path MoE, losses and two-stage optimization are retained. The specified instruction-generation procedure adds image-conditioned VLM generation and verification alongside LLM prompts, revises the teacher pool, and requests ten questions or pairs instead of an unrestricted number (v1 Figure 3; v2 Figures 5–6). The conflicting encoder descriptions do not establish an actual encoder replacement.

E1.justification: V2 adds evaluation on the public ultrasound dataset of Li et al. (2024b), identified as KMVE in Table 1, covering unseen breast, liver and thyroid data (Appendix G, Tables 11–12). This substantially extends evaluation beyond the retained internal seven-system dataset. Other datasets summarized in Table 1 are related-work comparisons, not additional evaluated benchmarks.

E2.justification: Tables 2–4 add Medgemma, LLaVA1.5, HuatuoGPT-Vision, Lingshu, LLaVA-Med, Qwen2.5-VL, LLaVA-NeXT and Gemma-3. The ultrasound-tuned LLaVA-OneVision and Qwen2-VL remain under shortened names, while their untuned columns disappear from these main comparisons. Case studies also add Lingshu, HuatuoGPT-Vision and Gemma-3, substantially broadening comparator coverage.

E3.justification: V2 introduces entity-based Hamming accuracy and macro precision, recall and F1, an external test explicitly excluded from training, a 3B configuration, and a six-expert setting. Internal testing retains 27,577 images, 3,000 reports and greedy decoding. Expert validation is now specified as 40,000 samples rather than 5% of ten-sample batches; this reported revision does not establish that review volume increased.

E4.justification: Appendix G adds a distribution-shift generalization test. Table 7 extends the expert-count ablation from 0/2/4 to 0/2/4/6 experts and adds training-cost evidence. Existing anatomical case studies gain additional comparator outputs. The routing and Grad-CAM analyses are largely retained and reflowed, rather than newly introduced.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-training-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or implemented significance tests. Both retain deterministic greedy decoding. V1's unsupported wording about statistically significant gains does not document a statistical procedure.

E6.justification: Matching baseline scores are revised: report-generation BLEU-1 for tuned Qwen2-VL changes from 43.72 to 46.29. EchoVLM-11B's VQA averages change from 26.52 to 30.13 BLEU-1 and 49.69 to 51.76 BERTScore, while its report-generation and diagnosis scores are largely retained. Numerous baseline, 3B, six-expert, entity-level and OOD results are added. These are reported-result changes, not established same-setting performance improvements.

T1.justification: The routing, autoregressive-loss and load-balancing equations retain their mathematical substance, with no new theorems, proofs or derivations. Replacing LN with RMSNorm in the block equations aligns the text with normalization already depicted in v1's architecture figure.

C1.justification: The central contributions—an ultrasound-specialized VLM, a multicenter dataset and instruction pipeline, and Dual-path MoE—remain. The abstract narrows the reported report-generation advantage over Qwen2-VL from 10.15/4.77 to 7.58/3.45 BLEU-1/ROUGE-1 points and explicitly emphasizes coverage of over 100 diseases or imaging findings.

C2.justification: V2 adds explanations concerning clinical entity correctness versus text similarity, external generalization, and the performance–cost trade-off favoring four experts. It specifically qualifies VQA performance against Lingshu. The vascular long-tail explanation, spurious-attention discussion and missed-nodule limitation largely retain their earlier meaning despite relocation.

D1.justification: V2 substantially expands documentation with hospital names, de-identification and ethics information, revised generation/verification prompts, filtering from 3.42 million instructions to 1.8 million pairs, 3B expert dimensions, and baseline full-parameter-tuning disclosure. Training times are added, and hardware changes from an H100 plus two A100s to eight A100s. The code/weights access statement remains unchanged; encoder prose and Table 9 remain inconsistent.

R1.justification: V2 adds a substantial ultrasound-dataset comparison covering works such as KMVE, EchoCLIP, EchoPrime, FetalCLIP and Sonomate, positioning EchoVLM within multimodal ultrasound research. Related work also expands to newer medical VLMs, including Medgemma, HuatuoGPT-Vision and Lingshu. These additions go substantially beyond bibliographic formatting changes.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, related work and several methodological and experimental passages are extensively rewritten. V2 introduces numbered sections and lettered appendices, reorganizes pipeline and architecture explanations, separates limitations, and translates retained Chinese case-study panels into English.

P2.justification: V2 redraws the framework overview and preliminary performance chart, replaces the anatomical dataset illustration with detailed distribution plots, and adds dataset, entity-evaluation and OOD tables. Main result tables expand into full-width, color-highlighted comparisons. Prompt diagrams are separated, the architecture gains a radar panel, and routing, heatmap and case-study figures are substantially rearranged.

improvement.justification: V1 supports its broad clinical claims mainly through two baseline families and internal text-similarity evaluations. V2 substantially strengthens that evidence with medical comparators, clinical entity assessment and an external generalization test (Tables 2–4, 8 and 10–12). Expanded data-provenance documentation and measured expert-scaling costs also improve assessability. Entity-extraction and external-test details remain terse, uncertainty is unreported, and conflicting encoder descriptions weaken reproducibility, but these limitations do not outweigh the substantial improvement in empirical support.
